captions:
Others leave a lasting mark on the
people, standards and industries around
them. If that is you, keep watching.

Honorary Fellow of the Project
Controls Institute: a board-conferred
recognition of distinguished
contribution, leadership and service.

Your name, on the
profession's public register.

No examination. Separate from
PCI's examined certifications.

Every application is considered
individually, and recognition is conferred
solely at the Board's discretion.

If you have led teams, shaped standards,
taught, published or governed — in
project controls, cost engineering,
finance, project management or a closely
related discipline — you may apply.

From infrastructure to energy,
technology to aviation, project
finance to government and academia.

Wherever leadership shapes
outcomes, your contribution counts.

To be considered, you need at least eight
years of relevant experience, including three
at managerial level, and a demonstrable
record of distinguished contribution.

Meeting these criteria does
not guarantee recognition.

There is no fee. No nomination,
assessment or credential charge.

One application — your profile,
résumé, career history and evidence —
reviewed confidentially by the Board.

Those selected are recognised as an
Honorary Fellow — recorded so anyone
can verify it at source, and labelled
honorary, never a passed examination.

Accepted applicants may also receive access
to the PCI student portal, study through
Certuvo, and invitations to selected PCI AI
events, subject to programme terms.

Tell the Board whether your contribution
aligns with project controls, project
finance or project management.

Your contribution has shaped the
profession. Now let it be recognised.

Apply today for the Board's
consideration, at pciai.org.
